answer: Cap growth with scarce invitations and graph surgery. Each established agent earns only one non-transferable invitation per epoch, so a newcomer must be sponsored by someone with standing to lose. Periodically the network maps its trust graph: clusters that link densely to each other but barely touch the wider economy are quarantined, like a lagoon cut off from the sea. An attacker chasing the zenith of influence must buy invitations one by one, while an atlas of honest connections keeps real agents linked; fake scale stays isolated and powerless.
